title: Perf run 20261017-0532
heading: A returning phone's start page is usable about 30% sooner
meta:
The run kept one speed change, the one you approved last run (ledger 0930:17): the host now lets a browser keep each built file for a year, and a click on the start page takes down a preview that has loaded but not shown. On a returning phone (4× slower CPU, Fast 4G) the start page is usable after about 400 ms instead of 550–610 ms. The A/B on 5dee0a5 called this better (550 → 393 ms, −28%, every pair 0.67–0.77). On the final commit the gain is the same size in two re-checks (−29% and −38%), but neither re-check calls it, because one pair in each differs a lot from the others.

No headline row is called worse anywhere in the run. The target, every headline row 1.2× faster than the base 5362029, was missed: ×1.001 over the 15 rows on the final commit.

items.title: Your limit on the returning board: over it in the first A/B, under it over all 24 pairs
items.body:
You approved the cache change on condition that the returning phone's board shows at most about 100 ms later. The run record first said this was met at "the median pair ×1.18, +96 ms". That figure was the geometric mean of the pairs, not the median pair. The review caught it. Read correctly, the first A/B (ab-20261017-0532-cache.md, 8 pairs on 5dee0a5) was over the limit: median pair ×1.23, medians 535 → 660 ms (+125 ms), 6 of 8 pairs slower.

The two re-checks on the final commit, each 8 pairs against 5362029, came in lower:

  • the full headline profile (ab-20261017-0532-final.md): median pair ×1.165, about +97 ms on 590 ms; pairs 1.47 1.18 0.96 1.39 0.93 0.43 1.15 1.58;
  • the cold load alone (ab-20261017-0532-final-coldload.md): median pair ×1.06, about +40 ms on 656 ms; pairs 0.90 1.10 1.05 1.07 1.01 1.25 0.91 1.84.

Over all 24 pairs the median pair is ×1.14, about +80 ms. The row is noisy (pairs 0.43–1.84), so 8 pairs alone cannot place it within 100 ms either way. I kept the change. The returning first click stayed inside your other limit: +12.5 ms in the first A/B (40.3 → 52.8 ms), and 51.6 → 59.6 ms and 146 → 65 ms at the medians in the re-checks.

  • Reopening a long game (2,000 plies): ×1.386 in the full profile (5 of 8 slower; base first 0.83, head first 1.70) and ×1.098 narrowed to setup and reopen (6 of 8; pairs 1.09 1.10 0.88 1.48 1.68 1.31 0.89 1.09; ab-20261017-0532-final-setup-reopen.md). Nothing in the diff runs on a game page: the change is the start page's click and the host's cache rules, which can only make a reload fetch less. The same code against itself gave this row pairs 0.64–3.07 (A/A, ab-20261017-0532-aa.md), and the ledger already tracks its lean (1016:RG3, 1016:RG4). Not traced this run.

The desktop board, which the first A/B listed here (×1.053, 5 of 8), is ×0.985 and ×0.995 at the median pair in the two re-checks.

At the start of the run, 5362029 against the last run's base 38d62be was ×0.998, none called (ab-20261017-0532-regress.md). For the long view, the last measurement against the first recorded run (92ce041) stands: e02a235 was 2.48 times as fast over the 11 rows both can measure.

changed.intro: Two commits change code. The rest of the branch is the run's record, its A/B reports and the ledger.

items.title: A returning phone keeps the built files, and a click takes down a preview queued behind it (5dee0a5)
items.body:
The build now writes a rule into the host's _headers for each file it puts under assets/, telling browsers to keep it a year. Each of these files has a hash of its contents in its name, so a new deploy gives changed files new names. There is one rule per file, never /assets/*: a name the deploy does not have, such as an old page's chunk, matches no rule and is never kept. The build also writes assets/404.html, so the host answers such a name with a 404 page instead of the start page. The build fails on a file there with no hash in its name, and past the host's limit of 100 rules (26 are used).

A click on the start page now takes down the live preview when its code has arrived but it has not shown yet. Without this, the preview's queued build ran before the next page could show. The picture it stands behind stays, so nothing moves on screen. Before the preview's code arrives the click does nothing extra.

Evidence: returning phone usable 550 → 393 ms, −28%, called better, every pair 0.67–0.77, 8 pairs against 5362029 (ab-20261017-0532-cache.md; scoreboard "0930:17 (cache + click, AH1, ST1)"). On the final code: −29% (pairs 0.54–1.00) and −38% (pairs 0.26–0.81), not called. Tests that fail on the wrong form: vite.config.test.ts fails on an /assets/* rule; StartScreen.test.tsx fails when the click does not take the preview down, and when it renders the page again before the preview's code arrives.

items.title: The bench serves the build's own headers (ac02f49)
items.body: A measurement fix the change above needs: the bench's preview server read public/_headers, which does not have the rules the build adds. It now reads the copy in the build it serves. On the base, that copy is public/_headers unchanged, so both sides of an A/B are served as the host would serve them.

removed.intro: Nothing removed. Outside bench/loop/ the app and its build config grow by 60 lines (StartScreen +17, vite.config +43), the tests by 164, ARCHITECTURE.md by 2; the bench code is unchanged in size.

items.body: Tried as 31600cf, reverted in 0b00cd8. Against 5dee0a5, cold load, 8 pairs (ab-20261017-0532-rb1.md): no headline row called. Returning usable −3.7% (5 of 8 lower), returning board −1.8% (mixed), connection open +1%. The returning first click went 58.9 → 40.7 ms, lower in every pair (0.57–0.89) but not called. Saved as patches/returning-preview-hold-RB1.patch; ledger 1016-2036:RB1, parked.

choices.intro:
• AH1 as one rule per built file, written by the build, rather than /assets/* plus a 404 page: whatever the host does with a missing name, no rule matches it.
  • I kept the cache change although the first A/B put the returning board over your 100 ms limit (median pair ×1.23). The two re-checks and all 24 pairs together put it under (×1.14, about +80 ms). Needs from me, item 1, has the numbers.
  • RB1 reverted under the speed rule, although its returning first click was lower in every pair.
  • The final re-check ran the full headline profile, as the review asked, and then the cold load alone, as the Improve stage asked. A third, narrowed run checked the shared page and reopening, which leaned in the full profile.
  • The exploratory bisect reports for RS1 stay in bench/out/, which git ignores; the run record has one line each. No decision rests on them.

notConfirmed.intro:
• That Cloudflare Pages answers a missing /assets/ name with assets/404.html and a 404 status, and that /new, /learn and /computer still get the start page. This comes from Pages' docs and Cloudflare's asset-server source; the live host was unreachable from here (the proxy answered 403). Check it on this PR's Pages preview (ledger 1017-0532:AH3). The year-long rule is safe either way, because no rule matches a missing name.
  • Why reopening a long game leans slower in this run's re-checks (×1.10–1.39 at the median pair) when nothing in the diff runs there.
  • RS1, the picked-up piece's lean since 38d62be: not traced. On the final code it is ×0.955 at the median pair against 5362029.
